note: Clip seconds are the PLAN. They are re-timed against the real master after generation; nothing downstream may assume they are final.

beats.why: The claim input must be readable and usable before anything moves. This is the longest still beat on purpose.
Arc past the lamp post, line up with the doors, glide in.
Dense interior move. More scroll distance so the banked sweep and the S-curve are readable rather than a blur.
Transition. Short and fast, no copy to read.
Weaving an aisle. focusX right of centre on mobile because the move turns right at the end.
Side door into the archive room, curving past the drawers.
The open card drawer. Slow: this beat carries the still-open line, which is the product's signature claim.
Out the rear door. Transition, no copy.
The 180 degree turn gets its own beat so it never has to share scroll with copy.
Backwards climb, the campus opening out.
Holds the final aerial while the closing copy and the claim input are read. hold -1 means the last frame.

chapters.ch-hero: Heard a health claim? Check it against the research.
chapters.ch-search: We search the published research, not the internet.
chapters.ch-studies: Up to eight real studies per claim. Every one linked.
chapters.ch-graded: Each study graded by what kind of evidence it is.
chapters.ch-open: And every verdict says what is still open.
chapters.ch-verdicts: Likely true. Likely false. It's complicated. And what's still open.
